title: Central simplicity and finite dimensionality descend from a matrix form
statement: Let K and L be fields with a K-algebra structure on L, and let A be a unital associative K-algebra. Let n be a nonzero natural number and suppose e:L tensor_K A ≃ Mat_n(L) is an L-algebra equivalence. Then A is central over K, its ring is simple, and A is finite dimensional over K. No Galois or algebraicity hypothesis on L/K is needed.

source.place: Tag 03R2, implication (4) to (1), generalized to any field extension; parent step 3

proof.text: The nonzero size makes Mat_n(L) nontrivial and simple. Transfer simplicity and finite dimensionality over L along the equivalence e. The inclusion A → L tensor_K A shows A is nontrivial. Module.Finite.of_finite_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat descends finite dimensionality to K.

For x central in A, Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight_map_center_le shows 1 tensor x is central in L tensor_K A. Under e it is a scalar matrix, by Algebra.IsCentral.mem_center_iff and the matrix centrality instance. Therefore 1 tensor x = l tensor 1 for some l in L. Module.Projective.exists_dual_eq_one gives a K-linear functional f on L with f(1)=1. Applying f tensor id and the left-unit tensor equivalence gives x=f(l) times 1. Thus the center is contained in the scalar subalgebra, which is precisely Algebra.IsCentral K A.

Use isSimpleRing_iff_isTwoSided_imp. For a two-sided ideal I, either I=top, or A/I is nontrivial by Ideal.Quotient.nontrivial_iff. In the latter case L tensor_K (A/I) is nontrivial by faithful flatness. The scalar extension of Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ K I has simple domain L tensor_K A, so RingHom.injective makes it injective. Module.FaithfullyFlat.lTensor_injective_iff_injective reflects injectivity to the quotient map. Its kernel is I; RingHom.injective_iff_ker_eq_bot and Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ_ker show I=bot.
